title: Coral Resilience Lab StepOnePlus™ qPCR Protocol for Symbiodiniaceae Detection
author: Mariana Rocha De Souza
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bvzbn72n

steps.title: Prepare primer and probe stocks
steps.instruction: Reconstitute lyophilized primers to a 100 µM stock, keep the stock at –20 °C and use on ice (store working dilutions at 4 °C, avoid freeze‑thaw). Dilute forward primers to 1 µM, reverse primers to 1.5 µM, and probes to 2 µM as shown in Table 1. Probes for Cladocopium (VIC) and Durusdinium (FAM) are multiplexed; host primers/probes for Montipora capitata and Pocillopora damicornis are also prepared.

steps.title: Prepare qPCR mastermixes
steps.instruction: Make two separate 1.5 mL tubes (one for Symbiodiniaceae, one for coral host) and keep all reagents on ice. For each well the mastermix composition is:

substeps.instruction: Symbiodiniaceae C & D (9 µL per well): 5 µL GTMM, 0.5 µL Symb C forward primer, 0.5 µL Symb C reverse primer, 0.5 µL Symb C probe, 0.5 µL Symb D forward primer, 0.5 µL Symb D reverse primer, 0.5 µL Symb D probe, 1 µL Hi‑Clone ddH₂O.
Coral host (9 µL per well): 5 µL GTMM, 0.5 µL host forward primer, 0.5 µL host reverse primer, 0.5 µL host probe, 2.5 µL Hi‑Clone ddH₂O.

Run each sample in duplicate or triplicate. Include three controls: Positive control (coral DNA known to contain both C and D symbionts), Negative control 1 (Hi‑Clone ddH₂O), Negative control 2 (extraction TE buffer).

steps.title: Calculate mastermix volumes for full plate
steps.instruction: If using a full 96‑well plate (92 usable wells), calculate total volumes for 46 Symbiodiniaceae wells and 46 host wells:

substeps.instruction: Symbiodiniaceae mix: 230 µL GTMM, 23 µL each Symb C forward, reverse, probe, 23 µL each Symb D forward, reverse, probe, 46 µL Hi‑Clone ddH₂O.
Coral host mix: 230 µL GTMM, 23 µL each host forward, reverse, probe, 115 µL Hi‑Clone ddH₂O.

steps.title: Plate mastermix and DNA samples
steps.instruction: Print a 96‑well template, label each well with sample ID and reaction type (S for Symbiodiniaceae, H for host). Keep DNA samples on ice in a micro‑centrifuge rack in the order they will be plated. Then:

substeps.instruction: Add 9 µL of the appropriate mastermix to the bottom of each designated well (use separate pipette tips for the two mixes).
Flick each DNA sample tube to mix, then add 1 µL of DNA to the side of the corresponding well (use a fresh tip for each sample).
Seal the plate with qPCR sealing tape and roll to ensure a tight seal.
Centrifuge the sealed plate at 10 000 g for ~10 s to spin DNA into the mastermix.
Inspect wells for correct liquid volume and absence of bubbles; if bubbles are present, flick the well and centrifuge again.

steps.title: Seal plate and centrifuge
steps.instruction: After adding DNA, seal the plate with qPCR sealing tape, roll the tape to ensure adhesion, then spin the plate at 10 000 g for about 10 seconds. Verify that all liquid is at the bottom of each well and that no bubbles remain.

steps.title: Run qPCR on StepOnePlus
steps.instruction: Place the sealed plate in the StepOnePlus thermocycler in the same orientation as loaded. Load the saved program named “TaqMan_Std”, set the reaction volume to 10 µL, and start the run.

steps.title: Export and save raw results
steps.instruction: When the run finishes, insert a USB thumb drive into the StepOnePlus, choose “Save Results”, and copy the .Taq file to the drive. Alternatively, on the connected computer select “Collect experimental results”, open the .Taq file in the StepOne software, and save the file as an Excel workbook.

substeps.instruction: Click “Setup”, then “Define Targets”. Add three targets (C, D, Host) and assign the correct fluorescent reporter dyes (VIC for C, FAM for D, etc., as in Table 2).
In “Define Samples”, list all sample names as they appear on the plate.
Go to “Assign Targets and Samples”, highlight wells, check the boxes for the appropriate target and sample name (you can assign targets to all wells at once, then assign sample names individually).
Open “Analysis Settings”, set Threshold = 0.01 and Baseline = 6‑23 for both C and D, then click “Apply Analysis Settings”.
Ensure “Show baseline” and “Show threshold” are enabled to view amplification curves.
Export the results: File → Export → Results, choose Excel format, name the file, and save.
Save the run settings (File → Save As) for future reuse and copy them to the USB drive.

steps.title: Process data in R
steps.instruction: Run the following R script (copy‑paste into an R console) to clean and analyse the exported Excel file:

substeps.instruction: library(ResourceSelection)  # for logistic regression if needed
# Set working directory to folder containing exported results
# Load raw data (assumes file named qPCR1.xls)
# Keep only relevant columns and convert Ct columns to numeric
mutate(c_mean = c_mean - fluo.C,               # Cunning et al. 2017
mcap_mean = mcap_mean - fluo.Mcap) %>% # Cunning et al. 2017
filter(is.na(rep))   # keep only rows without replication warning
# The object ‘cleaned’ now contains all calculated ratios, warnings, and proportions
# Proceed with statistical analysis or visualization as desired.
